item.text: I’m re-reading the current implementation with an eye for the next structural seam rather than surface cleanup. The biggest remaining issue is that traversal is still list-centric and order checks are scattered through recursion.

I’m refactoring traversal around a visitor-style API now. That removes repeated `TraversalOrder` branching during recursion and stops building intermediate lists unless a caller explicitly asks for one.
The traversal refactor is in place. I’m compiling and running it now to confirm the new visitor-based path preserved the tree’s behavior.
I’ve verified the behavior stayed the same. I’m pulling final line numbers so the summary can point directly at the new traversal API and the internal simplification it enabled.

Refactored traversal in [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:85) around a visitor-style API. The new `forEach(TraversalOrder, Consumer)` is now the central traversal entry point, and both `traverse(...)` and `joinTraversal(...)` delegate to it instead of each maintaining their own traversal flow.

This also let me remove the per-node `if` checks on `TraversalOrder` during recursion. Traversal now dispatches once at the top, then uses dedicated methods for preorder, inorder, and postorder at [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:183). That makes the recursion simpler, avoids unnecessary intermediate lists for string joins, and gives the tree a more flexible extension point for future callers that want to stream values directly.

Verification: `javac AVLTree.java AVLTreeDemo.java` succeeded, and `java AVLTreeDemo` still prints `30 20 10 25 40 50`.
